title.narrative: Shalom Centre for Conflict Resolution and Reconciliation -Office Set Up Support

description.narrative:
Shalom Centre for Conflict Resolution and Reconciliation (SCCRR) is a relatively new organisation but clearly builds on the work and reputation of the local church, missionary activity and development NGOs across northern Kenya. The added value of SCCRR initiative is that it brings a range of actors together in a new and meaningful way, building on the strengths of each with a view to creating local and sustainable solutions to the intractable nature of conflict in the region. Furthermore, SCCRR has been mandated to work for peace and conflict resolution in northern Kenya by 64 missionary groups working in the country, and enjoys the support of the Kenyan government authorities (nationally and local) and academic institutions in Nairobi
The overall problem this project seeks to address is the prevailing violence and conflict between the Turkana people and neighbouring ethnic groups, notably the Karimojong, Toposa, Dassenach, Samburu, Pokot, and Borana peoples. There is a long history of conflict between the Turkana and their neighbours that significantly impacts on the well being of the people and the possibility for socio-development across the region. Through a range of methodologies, the intervention will attempt to reduce the level of violent conflict (behavioural and structural) in the project site. While the conflict has been ongoing for hundreds of years, tensions between various groups are compounded by the increasing availability of weapons across the region, and indeed the fragile political situation in the whole of Kenya following the violent aftermath of the 2008 elections. The overall aim is to transform the current culture of conflict into one of peace. The project further aims at influencing national development and security policy towards the region that would lead to enhancing human security among poor and vulnerable communities in the Northern regions of Kenya.
